speaker: Mr Ang Wei Neng
text: asked the Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance whether he can provide an update on the progress of the Forward Singapore exercise and the plans ahead.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: This involves reviewing our existing assumptions and ideas on making Singapore a better home for our people, to see whether they remain valid.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: It also involves generating new ideas and policy thinking to address our challenges and seize new opportunities.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Since we launched the exercise in June, the response from Singaporeans in the many conversations with the 4G leadership team has been encouraging.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Over the next few months, we will deepen our conversations and partnerships with Singaporeans.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: We intend to do so in two ways.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: First, there will be more engagements for people to offer their own views and ideas, as well as to hear from others.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: These will span a wide range of topics, such as how to strengthen employability and create good jobs, make our living environment even better, strengthen our bonds to Singapore and with one another, and environmental sustainability, amongst others.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Some of these engagements will be held in our neighbourhoods and some in vernacular languages and different formats to better reach out to Singaporeans of different needs and preferences.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: These engagements will allow us to reflect on our values today and what we aspire to be in the future.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: They will sensitise us to the choices we have to make as a people, for ourselves, as well as the longer-term interest of future generations.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Second, we will invite people to go beyond just giving views, to also co-develop and implement solutions and policies together with the Government.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: For example, approaches like Citizens' Panels and Alliances for Action (AfA) bring people together to deliberate on issues they feel strongly about and, after robust discussions with one another and experts, recommend policy ideas to the Government.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Through AfA, stakeholders can also come together to take direct action in designing and implementing solutions.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: We hope to partner Singaporeans from all walks of life for this Forward Singapore exercise because everyone has a role to play, to build a better Singapore for all.

speaker: Mr Ang Wei Neng (West Coast)
text: We are very heartened to see that the Forward Singapore exercise is gaining momentum.

speaker: Mr Ang Wei Neng (West Coast)
text: One, I would like to ask Deputy Prime Minister Wong whether the issue of repealing section 377A of the Penal Code will be discussed at a Forward Singapore exercise before it is tabled at Parliament.

speaker: Mr Ang Wei Neng (West Coast)
text: And meanwhile, I also hope that the Government will not issue any major White Paper before the end of this exercise.

speaker: Mr Ang Wei Neng (West Coast)
text: But, to be sure, I am not referring to the Healthier Singapore White Paper that we will discuss tomorrow.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: But, of course, if there are views around society and our values and Singaporeans feedback this to us through our engagements and conversations, we will take in all of the feedback as part of the Forward Singapore engagements.
